title: The Benefits of PLP Moving into Mainstream Manufacturing
summary: Learn how panel-level packaging (PLP) boosts throughput, yields, and cost efficiency as it moves into mainstream manufacturing.
body_markdown:
Following parts 1 and 2 on panel-level packaging (PLP) cleaning challenges and market drivers, this third and final blog on PLP technology delves into how the industry will benefit from its commercialization.


Artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), medical and automotive applications require multi-die packaging. Moreover, most of these applications need very thin packaging with low power and minimized heat output.


The current technology uses wafer-level packaging (WLP), which builds up packages on top of a round substrate. As package sizes increase, the number of packages that can be manufactured on the round substrates is reduced, and yields can be impacted if the package is too close to the substrate edge.


For PLP, a square or rectangular substrate is used for building the package. More packages can fit on the substrate simply because of its geometric shape. This increases the number of packages per process chamber, which improves carrier utilization and, as a result, the throughput of the packaging supplier.


## Growing Package Sizes Spur Unique Challenges


As package sizes grow, fewer units can fit on each 300mm wafer, leading to increased edge losses, with the cost of each processing step being spread across fewer sellable packages. The result is a steady deterioration in wafer-level economics as module area expands. Panel processing addresses this by replacing the round wafer interposer with a rectangular substrate that can be several times larger in total area, improving the number of units per processing run and spreading fixed costs more efficiently.


To date, the market has not yet agreed upon a single panel size, delaying broad adoption of PLP. Several different panel sizes are currently used for the PLP process: 310x310mm, 510x515mm and 600x600mm. Due to its size, the 600mm2 panel would be optimal and potentially give the best yield, but its larger size also creates the most manufacturing challenges, including greater warpage risk.


Additionally, for wafer equipment manufacturers, the size is considerably larger than a 300mm wafer. The difference between wafer size and panel size means there is not a full equipment suite available; in some cases, manufacturers who are developing PLP lines need to kluge equipment together to create a process flow that fits their needs.


## ACM Research Adapts Wafer Cleaning Expertise for Panel Tool Development


ACM Research is one of the few companies that has been focusing on PLP equipment and processing. We’ve developed and begun production on three tools, with more in the pipeline. As we have already developed the wafer-handling system for all three panel sizes, we were able to adapt the process for panels as well.


Since a significant amount of our equipment is designed for single-wafer applications, we have adapted our technology for the required panel size, ensuring our panel process quality remains the same as that for wafers. Our product line offers process solutions for all three panel sizes with excellent uniformity and low contamination, leading to excellent yields for the manufacturers using our equipment.


## Key Technology Highlights


ACM has three processes in production at outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) manufacturers: an electrochemical plating (ECP) and polishing tool, a flux cleaning tool and an edge bevel tool. The ECP tool has a unique multi-anode system that enables deposition of metal layers with < 5% within-in-panel non-uniformity across all panel sizes. The vacuum technology in the Ultra C vac-p flux ensures the cleaning liquid thoroughly reaches all gaps, even in large panel substrates where traditional methods fall short. Combined with ACM’s proprietary isopropyl alcohol (IPA) drying technology, this comprehensive cleaning process prevents residues that could impair device performance.


The Ultra C bev-p tool’s innovative design ensures a precise bevel-removal process that remains confined to the bevel region, even on warped panels. This advancement is vital for maintaining the integrity of the etching process and achieving the high performance and reliability required by advanced semiconductor technologies. This process is crucial for preventing electrical shorts, minimizing contamination risks, maintaining the integrity of subsequent processing steps and ensuring the long-term reliability of devices.


## **PLP Tools** **In Action**


ACM actively works with OSAT research and development and has implemented all three advanced processes with excellent results. We have developed multiple processes for all panel sizes, enabling companies to test the waters with smaller panels and then move to larger panels. OSATs developing PLP processes have the opportunity to use fan-out packaging and then transfer their knowledge to panels for multiple multi-reticle packaging applications.


Fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP) is still in the development stage for AI, HPC, automotive and medical applications. Using PLP can increase throughput and yields, decrease costs and meet the strong demand of growing applications. To achieve the output and yields that end users are demanding, the industry will need to begin transitioning to PLP between now and 2029.
